name: blit_tile_run_to_screen
description: Copies a run of tiles into the screen buffer, each tile written as 16 rows of four interleaved bitplane words at 40-byte plane spacing, one word column per tile. The run is read from a byte list that stops at the terminator value 255, and each byte selects a tile from a fixed tile table.

name: blit_tile_run_lower_screen
description: Copies a run of tiles like its neighbouring routine, but the destination starts eight screen rows lower and at a constant base offset instead of the scroll-dependent one. The byte list ends at the terminator value 255.

name: advance_animated_sprite_list
description: Walks thirty animation records: each active record waits out its delay, then applies the next signed x and y step from its script. When the script reaches its end marker the record deactivates itself and the active count is decremented.

name: copy_wide_block_scroll_up
description: Copies an 88-row, ten-column block of four-plane words from a source offset chosen by the low four bits of the scroll offset into the screen. It then steps the scroll offset down by 640, resetting it to 1 when it reaches zero.

name: copy_wide_block_scroll_down
description: Copies an 88-row, ten-column four-plane block from a source offset chosen by the low four bits of the scroll offset into the screen. It then steps the scroll offset up by 640, using a step of 4 at one boundary value and resetting it to 1 at another.

name: blit_static_panel_to_screen
description: Copies a fixed 20-column, 16-row four-plane graphic from constant data into the screen at a constant offset plus the scroll offset. The source is never computed, so the same image is drawn every call.

name: copy_narrow_block_scroll_down
description: Copies an 88-row, seven-column four-plane block from a source offset chosen by the low four bits of the scroll offset into the screen. It then steps the scroll offset up by 640, with a step of 4 at one boundary value and a reset to 1 at another.

name: copy_narrow_block_scroll_back
description: Copies an 88-row, seven-column four-plane block like its neighbouring routine, then steps the scroll offset up by 640 with a step of minus 4 at one boundary value and a reset to 1 at another.

name: blit_static_strip_to_screen
description: Copies a fixed 13-column, 26-row four-plane graphic from constant data into the screen at a constant offset plus the scroll offset.

name: blit_static_block_to_screen
description: Copies a fixed eight-column, 111-row four-plane graphic from constant data into the screen, offset by the scroll offset plus a small constant.

name: build_bitplane_union_masks
description: Builds several mask buffers by OR-ing the four bitplane words of source graphics together, storing each combined word across the destination plane slots. The final pass stores the inverted OR for 880 words, giving a transparency mask.

name: run_blitter_masked_copy
description: Programs the blitter for a 112-line, 14-word copy using all four channels with a select-style minterm and full first and last word masks. It takes the source pointer from its caller, uses the scroll-dependent destination, and then waits on a status bit until the blit finishes.

name: draw_masked_sprite_block
description: Draws an 88-row, ten-column four-plane sprite into the screen: each destination word is ANDed with a per-row mask word and then ORed with the sprite word. Planes are 40 bytes apart and rows 160 bytes apart.

name: clear_strided_record_blocks
description: Writes zeros to the first 20 bytes of each of 352 records that are 40 bytes apart, starting at a fixed offset in the working buffer. The remaining bytes of each record are left untouched.

name: fade_sixteen_colors_toward_target
description: On every third call it moves each of sixteen colour words one step toward its matching target word, adjusting each of the three 4-bit channel fields independently. The step is one unit up or down per channel.

name: fade_eight_colors_toward_target
description: On every third call it moves each of eight colour words one step toward its matching target word, adjusting each of the three 4-bit channel fields independently. It is the eight-entry counterpart of its neighbouring fade routine.

name: copy_static_record_table_rows
description: Copies 96 rows of five-word records from a fixed table into a buffer at a scroll-dependent offset plus a constant. Source rows are 10 bytes apart and destination rows 40 bytes apart.

name: start_audio_channel_from_flags
description: Checks four flag bits in order and, for the first one set, enables that channel's interrupt, loads its sample pointer and length, then returns. Each of the four audio channels has its own fixed sample address and length.

name: silence_audio_and_dispatch
description: Zeroes the four audio channel volume registers and writes the audio control register, then performs an indirect call through a jump table indexed by the input value. The called handler is chosen by the input byte.

name: start_stream_and_call_handler
description: Stores two fixed constants into an object record, points its stream read pointer at the byte after the current table entry, and decodes one byte to form a second pointer. It then calls the handler whose address is held in the record.

name: start_stream_at_offset_four
description: Stores a fixed constant in the object record, points its stream read pointer at the byte after the entry found four bytes into the parameter block, and decodes one byte to form a handler pointer. It then calls that handler through a record field.

name: start_stream_at_offset_six
description: Stores a fixed constant in the object record, points its stream read pointer at the byte after the entry found six bytes into the parameter block, and decodes one byte to form a handler pointer. It then calls that handler through a record field.

name: reset_channel_state_records
description: Clears nine per-record state bytes, sets a word counter to 6 and two marker bytes to 255, and stores a handler pointer in one record field. It only writes values and contains no loops or reads.

name: update_audio_channel_streams
description: Advances the sound stream of each of the four audio channels once per call: it reads the next stream byte, looks up a period value from a table, and writes it to the period register. When a channel's counter expires it calls a handler, and volumes for channels zero and one are cleared while channels two and three take stored values.

name: setup_audio_stream_update
description: Stores the first two stream bytes into the audio record and then runs the per-channel period and volume update loop, calling a handler when a counter expires. The input is truncated, so only the setup and the start of the loop are recovered.

name: start_audio_update_loop_alt
description: Alternate entry into the same audio update loop as its neighbour: it stores one stream byte and starts the loop one byte later. The routine body is truncated in the input, so only the start is recovered.

name: store_first_field_and_dispatch
description: Stores the first input byte into one record field, then calls a handler selected from a jump table by the second input byte.

name: store_second_field_and_dispatch
description: Stores the first input byte into a different record field, then calls a handler selected from a jump table by the second input byte.

name: store_offset_pointer_and_dispatch
description: Reads a word from the input and stores the record-relative address it points to in one record field, then calls a handler chosen from a jump table by the following byte.

name: store_offset_pointer_second_field
description: Reads a word from the input and stores the record-relative address it points to in a second record field, then calls a handler chosen from a jump table by the following byte.

name: dispatch_by_stream_byte
description: Calls a handler selected from a jump table by the byte at the input pointer and the high byte of the input word. It does no other work.

name: store_stream_pointer_and_dispatch
description: Reads a word from the input, saves the stream position after it in one record field, and stores a flag byte in another. It then calls a handler chosen from a table indexed by a byte at a record-relative offset.

name: load_descriptor_and_dispatch
description: Copies two pointers and two words from a descriptor table, chosen by an input word, into the record. It then writes three fixed control words and dispatches through a jump table; the routine is not reached in the reference run.

name: load_descriptor_and_dispatch
description: Copies two pointers and two words from a descriptor table, chosen by an input word, into the record. It then writes three fixed control words and dispatches through a jump table.

name: update_audio_channel_state_partial
description: Partial audio channel update that stores a stream pointer and a counter-driven handler dispatch, then updates the period and volume of the remaining channels from lookup tables. The input is truncated, so the rest of the routine is not recovered.

name: run_audio_channel_update_loop
description: Sets two flag bytes and a control word, then runs the per-channel audio loop that compares stream bytes against a threshold and updates periods, volumes and handlers. The input is truncated after the loop head, so the full loop body is not recovered.

name: stop_audio_or_select_sequence
description: Reads a sequence byte: when it and the following byte are both negative, it clears the four audio volume registers and the playback counter and returns. Otherwise it picks a pointer from a lookup table using the byte and calls the handler stored in the record.

name: update_audio_channels_from_stream
description: Initialises flag bytes and a control word, stores a stream pointer from the first two bytes, then loops over the stream comparing each byte to a threshold and updating each channel's period, volume and handler counter.

name: update_audio_channel_counters
description: Updates the period, volume and counter fields of the audio channels from lookup tables, calling a handler when a counter goes negative. The routine is not reached in the reference run.

name: start_audio_stream_loop_fragment
description: Stores a pointer to the stream after a two-byte header and a counter byte, then starts the same per-channel update loop as its neighbours. It is not reached in the reference run and is truncated, so only its start is recovered.

name: start_audio_loop_counter_entry
description: Stores one stream byte as a counter and points the stream pointer one byte later, then enters the per-channel audio update loop. The loop body is truncated, so only its entry is recovered.

name: store_flag_byte_and_dispatch
description: Stores the first input byte in one record field, then calls a handler chosen from a jump table by the second byte.

name: store_channel_byte_and_dispatch
description: Stores the first input byte in a second record field, then calls a handler chosen from a jump table by the second byte.

name: store_record_pointer_and_dispatch
description: Reads a word from the input and stores the record-relative address it points to in a record field, then calls a handler chosen from a jump table by the following byte.

name: store_record_pointer_and_dispatch
description: Reads a word from the input and stores the record-relative address it points to in a different record field, then calls a handler chosen from a jump table by the following byte.

name: dispatch_by_stream_byte
description: Calls a handler selected from a jump table by the byte at the input pointer and the high byte of the input word. It does no other work.

name: store_stream_pointer_and_dispatch
description: Reads a word from the input, saves the stream position after it in a record field, and stores a flag byte in another. It then calls a handler chosen from a table; the routine is not reached in the reference run.

name: load_descriptor_and_dispatch
description: Copies two pointers and two words from a descriptor table into the record, writes three fixed control words including a different one from its neighbour, and dispatches through a jump table.

name: update_audio_channel_tail_fragment
description: Stores a stream byte and pointer, counts down one channel's counter, and either dispatches a handler when it expires or reloads that channel's period and volume from lookup tables. The routine is not reached in the reference run.

name: run_audio_channel_update_loop
description: Sets two flag bytes and a control word, stores a stream pointer, and runs the per-channel audio loop that compares stream bytes against a threshold and updates periods, volumes and handlers.

name: start_stream_and_call
description: Reads a sequence byte, using a negated offset back to a second byte when the first is negative, and sets the stream pointer and a record pointer from a lookup table. It then calls the handler stored in the record.

name: run_audio_stream_with_header
description: Stores a header byte, a counter byte and three flag bytes, then runs the per-channel stream loop that compares bytes against a threshold and updates periods, volumes and handlers. The routine is called from several places in the reference run.

name: store_stream_pointer_and_dispatch
description: Reads a word from the input, saves the stream position after it in a record field, and stores a flag byte in another. It then calls a handler chosen from a table indexed by a record byte; the routine is not reached in the reference run.

name: update_audio_channel_counters
description: Updates the period, volume and counter fields of the audio channels from lookup tables, calling a handler when a counter goes negative. The routine is not reached in the reference run.

name: start_audio_update_loop_fragment
description: Stores a flag byte and a stream pointer, then enters the per-channel audio update loop at its volume and period update. The routine is not reached in the reference run.

name: store_stream_pointer_and_dispatch
description: Reads a word from the input, saves the stream position after it in a record field, and stores a flag byte in another. It then calls a handler chosen by a table lookup.

name: clamp_level_and_dispatch
description: Adds a base level to the input byte, clamps the sum between a lower and an upper limit passed in as parameters, and stores it in a record field. It then calls a handler chosen from a jump table.

name: store_packed_offset_and_dispatch
description: Combines three input bytes into the low 24 bits of a longword whose top byte is kept from the previous value, and stores it as a record-relative address. It also stores a parameter word, then calls a handler selected by the fourth byte.

name: reload_channel_period_and_volume
description: Stores a stream byte and pointer, counts down a channel's counter, and when it is still nonzero reloads that channel's period and volume from lookup tables. The routine is not reached in the reference run.

name: run_audio_channel_update_loop
description: Sets two flag bytes and a different control word in the channel record, stores a stream pointer, and runs the per-channel audio loop that compares stream bytes against a threshold and updates periods, volumes and handlers. The routine is not reached in the reference run.

name: start_stream_and_call
description: Reads a sequence byte, using a negated offset back to a second byte when the first is negative, and sets the stream pointer and a record pointer from a lookup table. It then calls the handler stored in the record.

name: run_audio_stream_with_header
description: Stores a header byte, a counter byte and three flag bytes, then runs the per-channel stream loop that compares bytes against a threshold and updates periods, volumes and handlers. The control word differs from its neighbours.

name: reload_channel_period_and_volume
description: Stores a stream byte and pointer, counts down a channel's counter, and reloads that channel's period and volume from lookup tables while the counter is nonzero. The routine is not reached in the reference run.

name: start_audio_update_loop_fragment
description: Stores a flag byte, a counter byte and a stream pointer, then enters the per-channel audio loop at its comparison step. The routine is not reached in the reference run.

name: start_blitter_and_wait
description: Writes a fixed control word, a second control word from its input and a blit size derived from another input to the blitter registers, then waits on the blitter busy flag. The code comes from a disk region that no reference run loads.

key: Disk.2 bytes 0-5376 (code never loaded by a reference run):0:0000
name: stub_undecoded_disk_region
description: Only one instruction is recorded at the start of a raw disk region that no reference run loads, and no decompiled body is available. Nothing beyond that can be described from the facts.

key: Disk.2 bytes 402688-403712 (code never loaded by a reference run):0:0000
name: start_blitter_size_and_wait
description: Writes a blit size derived from its input to the blitter size register, then waits on the blitter busy flag. The code comes from a disk region that no reference run loads.

key: Disk.2 bytes 540672-541696 (code never loaded by a reference run):0:0000
name: wait_for_blitter_idle
description: Loops until the blitter busy flag clears, with no other register writes. The code comes from a disk region that no reference run loads.

key: Disk.2 bytes 758784-759808 (code never loaded by a reference run):0:0000
name: start_blitter_copy_and_wait
description: Sets the blitter destination pointer from an input longword, writes a fixed control word and a second control word from its input, sets a blit size, then waits on the busy flag. The code comes from a disk region that no reference run loads.

name: process_task_messages
description: Looks up the current task through the exec library, reads its state fields, and calls helper routines that use Forbid, ReplyMsg and Alert. Only part of the sequence is recovered from the pseudo-code.

name: invoke_two_function_pointers
description: Calls two library routines through function pointers at fixed negative offsets from a base register, one after the other, and then returns. Neither result is used.

name: call_library_with_cleanup
description: Calls a library routine and returns its result if it is nonzero. Otherwise it runs a helper and, when a pointer is valid, calls two library functions and then two cleanup calls on that pointer before returning the fixed value 100.

name: open_handle_and_configure
description: Obtains a handle from a fixed identifier and returns null if that fails. It then runs a sequence of calls that fill a local buffer and pass a 20-byte block from the caller, followed by an allocation-style call.

name: run_initialization_sequence
description: Runs a fixed sequence of library and helper calls with constant identifiers and stops on failure. Several results are compared with fixed error values, and the final result is checked against one specific error code.

name: open_resource_and_cleanup
description: Requests a resource by a fixed identifier and makes a fallback call if the request fails. It then passes the resource to a helper when one was obtained.

name: relink_records_and_allocate
description: Calls a helper, then copies four pointer fields between two records, relinking them as it goes. It then requests a block of 8000 units with a fixed flag word, makes a fallback call with a negative constant on failure, and makes one final call with 514.

name: busy_wait_then_call_zero
description: Counts up to its input in an empty loop with no body, then calls a library routine with a constant zero argument and returns. The loop only burns time.

name: pack_nibble_triples_to_words
description: Reads groups of three bytes through a library call and packs the high nibble of each byte into one 12-bit word per group. The number of groups is capped by a caller-supplied byte, and the routine returns zero or the failing call's result.

name: validate_and_copy_bitmap
description: Checks a bitmap descriptor's depth field and size against limits, computes word-aligned row sizes from its width, and copies rows in a loop. It returns negative error codes for bad or oversize input.

name: seek_twice_return_position
description: Returns minus five for non-positive input; otherwise it makes two seek calls on the handle with a zero offset and returns the second result, mapping a negative result to minus three.

name: initialize_descriptor_and_fill
description: Clears the fields of a descriptor, stores two input values in it, and calls a helper to fill it. It returns the fill call's negative error, minus four when fewer than eight entries were filled, or zero after a cleanup call.

name: update_delta_accumulator
description: If the structure pointer is set, it adds the change in a source value since the last update to a 32-bit accumulator field and stores the new value as the previous one. It always returns zero.

name: seek_and_update_offset
description: Seeks the handle in the structure by the requested byte count when that count is positive, and adds the count to the structure's offset field on success. It returns zero on success and minus nine when the seek fails.

name: parse_iff_chunk_header
description: Skips the unread rest of the current chunk plus any word padding, then reads and validates the next chunk header. Group identifiers CAT, LIST and FORM are accepted at the top level, and bad sizes, read failures and unexpected identifiers return negative codes.

name: read_length_field_into_record
description: Reads a four-byte field into the record through a helper and stores the result in a length slot when the read succeeds. It returns the stored length value.

name: verify_and_read_chunk
description: Checks that the requested length is non-negative and no larger than the bytes remaining, then reads that many bytes through a helper. On success it advances two position counters by the length; otherwise it returns a negative status such as minus six, minus eight, minus nine or minus three.

name: reject_prop_chunk_result
description: Calls a helper and compares its result with the identifier PROP. On a match it records minus nine in a status field and returns minus nine; otherwise it returns the helper's result unchanged.

name: configure_two_resource_slots
description: Requests two resources by fixed identifiers, and when both succeed it sets a status value of minus one in each and stores two fixed values in their pointer fields. It then sets a flag bit in the global state.

name: link_identifier_chain_and_scan
description: Chains seven helper calls that link consecutive identifiers, then reads a value from a helper and runs a byte-scanning loop with a counter. Only part of the loop body is recovered from the decompiled code.

name: unpack_run_length_row
description: Decodes one row of run-length encoded bytes: a negative count repeats the next byte, while other counts copy literal bytes, and the requested length is decremented as it goes. It updates both pointers and returns a flag saying whether the full length was produced.

name: read_table_entry_pair
description: Looks up a record by the input index in a global pointer table, then copies its 16-bit values at offsets 22 and 20 into two global variables. The interrupt registers are listed in the facts but are not written in the pseudo-code.

name: read_table_entry_word
description: Looks up a record by the input index in the same global pointer table and copies its 16-bit value at offset 22 into a global variable, twice in succession. The interrupt registers are listed in the facts but are not written in the pseudo-code.

name: read_table_entry_word
description: Looks up a record by the input index in the global pointer table and copies its 16-bit value at offset 20 into a global variable. The interrupt request register is listed in the facts but not written in the pseudo-code, and the routine is not reached in the reference run.

name: store_indirect_result_in_record
description: Looks up a record by the input index in the global pointer table, calls a routine through a pointer at a fixed negative offset from the global base, and stores its result at offset 24 of the record. It returns the two input registers combined.

name: call_indirect_via_global_table
description: Calls a routine through a pointer at a fixed negative offset from the global base, then returns the two input values combined into one 64-bit result. The routine is not reached in the reference run.

name: invoke_indirect_through_global
description: Calls a routine through a pointer at a fixed negative offset from the global base and returns the two input values combined into one 64-bit result.

name: call_indirect_from_global
description: Calls a routine through a pointer at a different fixed negative offset from the global base, then returns the two input values combined into one 64-bit result. The routine is not reached in the reference run.

name: run_routine_four_times
description: Calls one routine four times in a row with no arguments and returns.

name: run_routine_four_times
description: Calls one routine four times in a row with no arguments and returns.

name: call_routine_six_times
description: Calls one routine six times in total: once before a four-pass loop and once after it. The loop calls the same routine each time, with no arguments.

name: initialize_audio_device
description: Performs one-time setup of the audio device: it allocates a 68-byte block on first use, sets its signal fields, calls a helper to create the port, and opens audio.device through the block. It returns zero on success and codes one to three for the failed stage, then makes two final calls.

name: allocate_read_and_free_block
description: Allocates a 272-byte block, aligns a working pointer inside it, and passes that pointer through two helper calls. It reads a longword at offset 124 as its result, then releases the helper resource and the block.

name: init_slot_control_block
description: Frees any existing block in the slot, allocates a 64-byte control block, and stores the input value and fixed constants in it when a second allocation succeeds. It returns zero early if the earlier audio setup has not finished, and releases partial allocations on failure.

name: chain_calls_through_global_table
description: Chains three helper calls and returns zero if any stage fails. On success it makes a final call using a pointer taken from the global table at the index given by the second input, releases the result, and returns one.

name: clone_object_from_table
description: Copies a source table entry into an empty destination slot when the source exists. It allocates a 64-byte block, copies the first longword and several fields from the source record, and sets the top bit of one flag field; it returns zero when it cannot proceed.

name: free_entry_and_cleanup
description: Frees the block in a table slot. When its top flag bit is clear it first frees the buffer the block points to, then frees the 64-byte slot block and clears the table entry.

name: run_table_setup_loops
description: Makes twenty calls that each pass a global-table address computed from a helper result, then calls a routine for each index up to a stored count. It finally forwards its two inputs to one more call.

name: check_signal_and_dispatch
description: Reads the signal mask for two signal bits, returning zero when neither is set. When set, it calls a routine with fixed codes, one of two codes chosen by which bit is set, iterates calls up to a global counter, and returns the result of one final call.

name: run_table_setup_loops
description: Makes twenty calls that each pass a global-table address computed from a helper result, then calls a routine for each index up to a stored count. It finally forwards its two inputs to one more call.

name: find_unused_table_entry
description: Scans a table of 24-byte entries from the global base until it finds one whose flag byte is zero before the end of the table. It passes the inputs and that entry to a helper and returns the result, or zero if no entry is free.

name: find_unused_table_entry
description: Scans a table of 24-byte entries from the global base until it finds one whose flag byte is zero before the end of the table. It passes the inputs and that entry to a helper and returns the result, or zero if no entry is free.

name: find_unused_table_entry
description: Scans a table of 24-byte entries from the global base until it finds one whose flag byte is zero before the end of the table. It passes the inputs and that entry to a helper and returns the result, or zero if no entry is free.

name: parse_open_mode_string
description: Parses an fopen-style mode string: the first letter selects read or write, the second selects binary or text, and a plus sign requests update. It releases any previously opened state, opens through a helper with fixed flags, and returns a record pointer or null on failure.

name: clear_object_links
description: Clears the link state of an object record: when one flag bit is set it makes a helper call, and when the middle flag bits are clear and a stored value is nonzero it releases that value. It then zeroes the two link fields and the flag byte, and finally calls a helper with a byte stored in the record.

name: expand_format_string
description: Expands a printf-style format string into a destination buffer one byte at a time. A doubled percent sign writes a single percent, other conversions are handled by a helper, and once the buffer count runs out each byte is passed to a second helper, using a 256-byte stack buffer.

name: read_byte_table_with_refill
description: Copies bytes from a buffered source into a destination in blocks of the given size, repeated for the given count. It calls a refill helper when the source buffer runs out and stops early on an end-of-data marker, returning the number of complete blocks copied.

name: get_slot_pointer_checked
description: Returns a pointer into the global slot table for the input index when the index is in range and the slot's top flag bit is set. It makes an optional helper call first when a global flag is set, and otherwise sets the error variable to nine and returns null.

name: get_slot_pointer_checked
description: Returns a pointer into the global slot table for the input index when the index is in range and the slot's top flag bit is set. It makes an optional helper call first when a global flag is set, and otherwise sets the error variable to nine and returns null.

name: open_slot_with_mode_flags
description: Finds the first unused slot in the table; when none is free it sets the error variable to twenty-four and returns minus one. Otherwise it writes mode flag bytes into the slot, opens through library calls with a mode chosen from the flags, and stores the handle in the slot.

name: clear_status_flag_and_recurse
description: Calls another routine with the first argument unchanged, a flags word made from the input's top bit plus fixed open flags of 769, and the input with its top bit cleared. It returns nothing and is not reached in the reference run.

name: transfer_slot_data_checked
description: Looks up a slot by its index and, for a non-negative byte count, passes the slot's handle with the buffer and count to a helper. A helper failure records the library error and sets the error variable to five, while a bad count or missing slot sets it to twenty-two and returns minus one.

name: transfer_slot_data_with_seek
description: Looks up a slot like its neighbour and passes its handle with a buffer and count to a helper. When a flag bit is set it first makes an extra call with a zero offset and mode two, and errors set the error variable as the neighbour does.

name: transfer_then_reset_slot_position
description: Looks up a slot and, for an index below three, passes its handle with a buffer and a stored per-index value to a helper. A failure records the library error and sets the error variable to twenty-two, and the routine ends with a final call on the handle using zero arguments.

name: close_handle_if_flag_clear
description: Looks up a slot and returns minus one if it is missing. When the slot's flag bit four is set it returns zero without closing anything; otherwise it closes the handle stored in the slot through a library call, clears the slot's first byte, and returns zero.

name: check_call_or_record_error
description: Calls a helper with its input and returns zero on success. On failure it records the library error, sets the error variable to two, and returns minus one. The routine is not reached in the reference run.

name: store_library_call_result
description: Passes the address of the global block and the fixed value 1005 to a library call, then stores the returned value in a global variable.

name: read_pending_byte_or_fetch
description: Returns a pending byte held in a global variable and clears it, otherwise reads one byte through a helper. It makes helper calls first, depending on two global values, and the routine is not reached in the reference run.

name: read_frame_byte_via_helper
description: Reads one byte into a local slot of the caller's frame through a helper, then returns that byte. The routine is not reached in the reference run.

name: read_byte_with_helper_checks
description: Makes optional helper calls depending on two global values, then reads one byte through a helper into its argument and returns that byte.

name: fill_buffered_read_state
description: Returns minus one when the status bits are set, and otherwise initialises an empty read buffer through a helper. It then calls a helper for the next value, records an error bit when that call is negative, and updates the state byte.

name: write_byte_buffered_with_flush
description: Writes a byte into a buffer while its counter allows, and when the counter runs out it passes the byte to a flush helper. It sets state flag bits from the helper results and returns the all-ones error value when the status bits are set.

name: reset_target_flags
description: If the structure has no pointer or its bit eight flag is set, it obtains a new value from a helper using a global argument and stores it in two fields. On failure it sets the error variable to twelve and returns minus one; on success it clears two status bits and zeroes two counters.

name: allocate_block_with_header
description: Requests a block sized to the input plus twelve bytes, stores the requested size at a fixed offset inside the block, and registers the block through a helper with a global value. It returns the block address plus twelve, or zero if the allocation fails.

name: return_nonzero_or_minus_one
description: Calls a helper with its input and returns that value if it is nonzero, otherwise returns minus one. The routine is not reached in the reference run.

name: return_minus_one
description: Returns the constant minus one and does nothing else. The routine is not reached in the reference run.

name: link_new_node_into_list
description: Inserts a new node at the tail of a doubly linked list: it copies the old tail into the node, clears its forward link, points the old tail's link at it, and sets the list head when the list was empty.

name: call_routine_with_value_twice
description: Passes its single input to another routine twice, as both arguments, and returns without further work.

name: find_or_allocate_sized_block
description: Returns null for a non-positive request. Otherwise it searches a size-ordered list for a block of the requested size, removing an exact match, and when none is found it requests a new block through helper calls and returns it, or null if that fails.

name: call_routine_args_twice
description: Passes its first argument and its second argument twice to another routine, then returns.

name: insert_or_update_list_node
description: Inserts a node into a list anchored by a global variable at a position computed by a helper, or adds the count to an existing node at that position. It returns zero on success and minus one when the count is not positive.

name: copy_string_to_buffer
description: Computes a destination inside the buffer by adding a helper result to the first argument, copies bytes from the source until a zero byte or the length limit is reached, writes a terminating zero, and returns the first argument.

name: count_string_bytes
description: Counts the bytes from the given offset up to the first zero byte and returns that count.

name: process_table_entries_then_call
description: Walks the global table of six-long entries and calls a helper on each entry that is in use and lacks flag bit four. It then makes one final call with its two inputs.

name: process_table_entries_then_call
description: Walks the global table of six-long entries and calls a helper on each entry that is in use and lacks flag bit four. It then makes one final call with its two inputs.

name: parse_and_dispatch_keyword
description: Skips a leading minus sign, flagged characters, a dot and an optional letter l, then searches a table of nine keyed entries for the remaining value. It calls the matching handler and returns zero when no key matches.

name: format_output_characters_partial
description: Fragment of a formatted-output routine: it sets a result flag, clamps a width count to a field value, and copies characters into the output buffer one at a time while the count stays nonnegative. The routine is not reached in the reference run and the pseudo-code is truncated.

name: fill_padding_characters_partial
description: Fragment of a formatted-output routine: it sets a result flag, clamps a width count against a field value, and writes a fill character into the output buffer while the remaining count stays nonnegative. The routine is not reached in the reference run.

name: pad_output_before_text
description: Fragment of a formatted-output routine that clamps a width count against a field value and writes padding characters into the output buffer. The routine is not reached in the reference run.

name: fill_padding_and_return_length
description: Writes fill characters into the output buffer while the remaining count stays nonnegative, stores the final output position in a result field, and returns the count plus one. The routine is not reached in the reference run.

name: fill_and_copy_formatted_text
description: Writes fill characters, then copies source bytes into the output buffer while a second count stays nonnegative. It stores the final output position in a result field and returns the count plus one. The routine is not reached in the reference run.

name: copy_formatted_text_bytes
description: Copies source bytes into the output buffer while the count stays nonnegative, stores the final output position in a result field, and returns the count plus one. The routine is not reached in the reference run.

name: copy_value_and_increment_counter
description: Stores a local output position through a pointer argument and returns a counter field plus one. The field offsets are frame-relative, and the routine is not reached in the reference run.

name: convert_number_with_precision
description: Fragment of a number-formatting routine: it defaults the precision to six when unset, clamps it to nineteen, and calls a conversion helper with the precision plus one. The routine is not reached in the reference run.

name: convert_number_digits
description: Fragment of a number-formatting routine that calls a conversion helper with the current precision plus one and stores the digit count and sign. The routine is not reached in the reference run.

name: compute_number_field_width
description: Fragment of a number-formatting routine that computes the output width from the precision and the magnitude of the value, adding width when the magnitude passes 99 and 999. The routine is not reached in the reference run.

name: pad_number_field_width
description: Finishes the width calculation for a formatted number, adding room when its magnitude passes 99 and 999, and writes padding characters while the remaining width allows. The routine is not reached in the reference run.

name: pad_number_field_left
description: Adds width when the magnitude passes 99 and 999 and writes padding characters into the buffer when the field has room. The routine is not reached in the reference run.

name: emit_sign_and_digits
description: Writes a minus sign when the flag is set, then emits digit characters from a source one at a time, writing zero once the digit count is exhausted. The routine is not reached in the reference run.

name: emit_digits_with_zero_fill
description: Fragment of the number formatter: a loop writes one digit from the source, or a zero once the digit count is exhausted, then writes padding while the field has room. The routine is not reached in the reference run.

name: emit_zero_digits_and_pad
description: Fragment of the number formatter: it writes a zero character, then repeats the padding loop while the field has room. The routine is not reached in the reference run.

name: emit_integer_then_decimal_point
description: Fragment of the number formatter: it writes integer digits from a source, substituting zeros when the digit count is exhausted, then writes a decimal point when a precision remains. The routine is not reached in the reference run.

name: emit_fraction_digits_with_padding
description: Fragment of the number formatter: it writes zeros and a decimal point when needed, then emits fractional digits while the precision allows. The routine is not reached in the reference run.

name: emit_fraction_digits
description: Fragment of the number formatter: it writes a decimal point when a precision remains, then emits fractional digits from a source, using zeros once it is exhausted. The routine is not reached in the reference run.

name: pad_fraction_with_zeros
description: Fragment of the number formatter: it writes zero characters and pads the field while the precision and width counts allow. The routine is not reached in the reference run.

name: emit_leading_digit_and_point
description: Fragment of the number formatter: writes one digit from a source or a zero, then a decimal point, then fractional digits while the precision allows. The routine is not reached in the reference run.

name: emit_zero_point_and_fraction
description: Fragment of the number formatter: writes a zero and a decimal point, then emits fractional digits while the precision allows. The routine is not reached in the reference run.

name: emit_exponent_notation
description: Fragment of the number formatter that writes an uppercase E and a sign, followed by exponent digits with zero substitution. The routine is not reached in the reference run.

name: emit_exponent_sign_and_digits
description: Writes an uppercase E, then a minus or plus sign according to the exponent, and starts a loop over up to eleven exponent digit positions. The routine is not reached in the reference run.

name: emit_exponent_digits_from_buffer
description: Writes a plus sign, converts exponent digits one at a time into a temporary buffer until the value reaches zero, then copies them to the output. The routine is not reached in the reference run.

name: copy_pending_bytes_return_length
description: Copies a pending fill byte into the output buffer while the count allows, stores the final output position, and returns a counter plus one. The routine is not reached in the reference run.

name: copy_value_and_increment_counter
description: Stores a local output position through a pointer argument and returns a counter field plus one. The field offsets are frame-relative, and the routine is not reached in the reference run.

name: copy_bytes_overlap_safe
description: Copies a block of bytes of the given length, choosing forward or backward order so that overlapping source and destination regions are copied correctly.

name: compute_signed_magnitude_division
description: Divides two signed 32-bit values by restoring division over their magnitudes, giving the quotient a sign taken from the XOR of the inputs. It returns zero when the divisor is zero.

name: return_without_action
description: Decompiles to a bare return with no effect, although the facts record 31 instructions for this block, so it is an empty stub.

name: shift_bits_into_result_pair
description: Shifts bits out of the input one at a time into a result over ten steps, with a zero magnitude returning zero, and returns a 64-bit pair of the result and the remaining input. The routine is not reached in the reference run.

name: shift_sign_bits_to_result
description: Shifts the ten top bits of the second input into the first input one at a time, then returns the first input's result with its top bit set. The routine is not reached in the reference run.

name: run_wide_math_on_record
description: Clears two 16-bit fields of a record and then makes a sequence of helper calls on 64-bit values, storing parts of the result back into the record. Only the start of the logic is recovered from the decompiled body, and the routine is called but not reached in the reference run.

name: store_split_longword_fields
description: Writes the low and high 16-bit halves of a longword into two record fields, then makes helper calls on a 64-bit value. Only the start of the routine is recovered, and it is not reached in the reference run.
